name: Express-collector corridor planning study — Canada TAC planning (Toronto context, PD-licensed portal)

metadata.name: Highway 401 Express-Collector Corridor Study (context analog)
metadata.description: Planning-stage safety review of express-collector lane management along a major urban freeway corridor, including interchange spacing and weaving assessment.
metadata.scheme_summary: Re-striping of express-collector transfer lanes; revised interchange access permissions; corridor signage rationalisation; no new rights-of-way.

design_criteria.value: TAC geometric design guide for Canadian roads; ministry freeway design supplement.

design_volume_traffic_characteristics.value: AADT 420,000 across the corridor; peak-hour transfer volumes from loop detectors.

route_choice_project_scope.value: Lane-management restriping only; no mainline realignment; transfer-lane permissions revised at three interchanges.

access_management_adjacent_developments.value: No changes to adjacent-development access; ramp terminals unchanged.

network_continuity_constraints.value: Ministry corridor plan records express-collector transfer continuity retained through all three interchanges; municipal network-continuity register records the middle-interchange transfer discontinued pending ramp-terminal reconfiguration.

provenance.license: Public domain (PD-self per Commons extmetadata verified 2026-08-22); Toronto OGL context via open.toronto.ca licence text
provenance.extractor: ORCH used the PD Basketweave diagram (Highway 401 express-collector multi-level weaving) as the geometric context narrative and shaped a TAC planning-stage Project per EV-CA-006 stage terminology.

expected_findings_baseline.location: Express-collector transfer points at three interchanges
expected_findings_baseline.scenario: Recorded corridor inputs show AADT 420,000 with transfer-lane permissions revised at three interchanges while corridor signage is rationalised at the same time; simultaneous unfamiliar lane assignments across the corridor risk late, erratic transfers whose collisions would appear elsewhere along the route during the transition. Vulnerable road users acknowledged: the express-collector mainline is a controlled-access facility carrying no pedestrians or cyclists, so VRUs are not applicable to this finding and road users are scoped to vehicle occupants.

statement.text: Stage the express-collector transfer-permission and signage changes sequentially so drivers are never confronted with simultaneous unfamiliar lane assignments across the corridor during the transition.

evidence.quote: minimise potentially negative safety impacts both within and outside the project limits, i.e. to avoid introducing collisions elsewhere along the route or on the network.

assumptions.text: Detector-based volumes represent typical peak demand.

confidence.label: medium
confidence.basis: Transition-conflict mechanism is labelled inference over recorded corridor volumes and change scope.

expected_findings_baseline.rationale: ORCH-as-judge baseline: decision-load mechanism inferred from recorded simultaneous restriping and signage rationalisation; staging logic grounded in the audit objectives quote.
expected_findings_baseline.recommendation: Introduce changes one interchange per quarter with before/after speed-differential monitoring.

expected_findings_baseline.scenario: Recorded network-continuity inputs conflict: the ministry corridor plan retains express-collector transfer continuity through all three interchanges while the municipal network-continuity register discontinues the middle-interchange transfer pending ramp-terminal reconfiguration, so the planning scope boundary cannot be confirmed; an unresolved boundary risks the audit excluding movements whose traffic redistributes to interchanges outside the project limits. Vulnerable road users acknowledged: the controlled-access mainline carries no pedestrians or cyclists, but continuity outcomes propagate to downstream arterials where VRUs travel; no VRU-specific exposure is asserted within this corridor question.

statement.text: Reconcile and consistently document the conflicting ministry and municipal network-continuity records before the planning recommendation is finalised — per the Alberta §5.6.2 discipline that responses to audit matters must choose accept / conditionally-accept-with-modifications / reject with documented reasons (EV-CA-038) — so the practice of undertaking and reporting the Planning Stage RSA rests on clearly specified scope records addressing safety for all road users.

evidence.quote: The project design team must provide a response report to the road safety audit within a reasonable period of time determined in consultation with Alberta Transportation. In preparing the response report, the project team should consult with the project sponsor. Possible responses are: 1. Accept in full and implement changes to project 2. Conditionally accept with modifications. The response report should document the reasons for the modifications 3. Reject with reason

It is important that a clear procedure for managing and organising road safety audit is established, and that the practice of undertaking and reporting road safety audit is clearly specified, and that the actions are fully and consistently documented.

confidence.label: high
confidence.basis: Conflicting state recorded directly in inputs; Alberta §5.6.1–5.6.2 (EV-CA-038) mandates response reports with documented reasons for modifications/rejections and filing of all documents, so an unresolved inter-register conflict is a process non-conformity rather than judgment.

expected_findings_baseline.rationale: Process-style compliance question surfaced by recorded input conflict; the reconciliation duty is grounded verbatim in EV-CA-038 (documented reasons required for any modification/rejection; reports filed for retrieval), with EV-CA-003 supplying the general documented-procedure duty. Completeness consequence framed from the all-road-users definition rather than an asserted collision mechanism.
expected_findings_baseline.recommendation: Reconcile the ministry corridor plan and municipal network-continuity register records with the ministry planning office, documenting the resolution reasons per the §5.6.2 response discipline, and record whether the resolved scope keeps corridor-wide continuity effects inside the audit boundary.

notes: conflicting network_continuity_constraints exercises the blocking 'conflicting' MI path on the CA pack (R-CA-NETWORK-CONTINUITY-RESOLVED, deterministic since 2026-08-24; coverage pinned by tests/domain/gf10-mi-path.test.ts). Fills the corpus coverage gap noted as thin for Canada.
